title = Advanced Training: Armor: Panzer 38(t)

# Spawn tanks at 60.3.39 N, 6.32..38 W facing 270 (West) # -314230.38 3603625.27 101.34 # facing front: -1.57 back: 1.58
1.0.label = Introduction
1.1.label = The Panzer 38(t)
1.1.alert.modal = This is the Panzer 38(t), one of the most common German tanks. It has three playable crew positions: driver and commander/gunner. Most tanks also have a loader modeled but that position can only look around within the turret. 1.1.alert.camera = 0,5,45,360,0,0,10 // pan around
2.0.label = The Driver
2.1.label = Driver's View 2.1.alert = This is position 1: the driver. From here you control the movement of the vehicle. The driver's view is limited through his view port.[NL][NL]Press {gunsightview} to improve the view. 2.1.alert.camera = internal 2.1.complete.modal = You can use {gunsightview} to toggle between the zoomed in view of the slit and the normal cockpit view.
2.2.label = Button up the Driver 2.2.alert = The Panzer 38(t)'s view port is protected by armored glass, which limits the view.[NL][NL]Press {canopycontrol} to lift the armored glass. 2.2.complete.modal = The view is improved but the driver is slightly more exposed to enemy fire.
2.3.label = Engine Status 2.3.alert = Press {instrumentview} to view your instruments. 2.3.complete.modal = Here you can see various gauges depending on the tank. Examples are: motor temperature, engine RPMs, and possibly other information like turret orientation.
2.4.label = Gear Shifting 2.4.alert.modal = All ground vehicles begin play with their engines off and in neutral gear.[NL][NL]They all have 1 or more forward gears and a single reverse gear. 2.4.alert1 = In order to move, you must put the vehicle in gear and use the gas.[NL][NL]To see what gear you are in, enable the Vehicle Status display by pressing {showstats}. 2.4.complete = Good, this displays the current gear the vehicle is in (N, or "neutral" when beginning). 2.4.complete.hilite = readout,target
2.5.label = Start the Engine 2.5.alert = Press {gunsightview} to look back through your driver's view port.[NL][NL]Start the engine by pressing {engstart}. 2.5.complete = Excellent!
2.6.label = Shift into First Gear 2.6.alert = Lower gears have more power and are useful for starting off or climbing slopes. Higher gears let you go faster but don't have much power so use them as you build speed on roads.[NL][NL]{shiftdown} and {shiftup} control the vehicle's gear.[NL][NL]Press {shiftup} to enter first gear. 2.6.alert.hilite = readout,target
3.0.label = Drive to Tank Firing Range
3.1.label = Movement Controls 3.1.alert.modal = Once your tank is in gear, you can use {gas.10.4} to move forward (or backward if in reverse). 3.1.alert1.modal = Use {leftbrake.10.4} to steer left and {rightbrake.10.4} to steer right. {bothbrake.10.4} will slow the tank. 3.1.alert2 = A series of waypoints will lead you to the Tank Firing Range. Drive through each waypoint to complete this part of training.[NL][NL]Use {gas.10.4} to accelerate.[NL]Use {bothbrake.10.4} to brake.[NL]Use {leftbrake.10.4} and {rightbrake.10.4} to steer left and right.
3.2.label = Turning 3.2.alert = Coming up is your first turn. As you approach the turn, use {bothbrake.10.4} to slow the tank if needed.[NL][NL]Use {leftbrake.10.4} and {rightbrake.10.4} to navigate the turn to the right.
3.3.label = Offroad Driving 3.3.alert = On the left side of this straight away is a set of bumps. Feel free to go over them or around them.[NL][NL]The next waypoint takes you offroad.
3.4.label = Choose Position 3.4.alert = Stop at the next waypoint. Use {bothbrake.10.4} to slow the tank to a stop.
3.5.label = Hull Down 3.5.alert.modal = A berm lines the road ahead separating you from the Tank Firing Range targets. 3.5.alert1.modal = Your tank's armor is thickest in the front and weakest in the rear.[NL][NL]Keep that in mind when positioning your tank. 3.5.alert2.modal = You can use berms, hills or even buildings to provide additional cover from enemy fire. This is commonly called "hull-down" and simply means that your hull is partially protected by the terrain because the enemy can't see or hit it. 3.5.alert3.modal = To be successful in armored combat, you must use both of these ideas.
3.6.label = Firing Position 3.6.alert = Take up a firing position against the berm next to the other tank.[NL][NL]Make sure your tank is facing north, which is downrange.[NL][NL]Take care not to drive up on the berm. If this was actual combat, that would expose more of your hull to enemy fire. 3.6.complete.camera = -90,10,20,-90,-8,0,5 3.6.complete.modal = Excellent, you are now in a hull down firing position.
# Follow the Waypoints # SW corner of track: "Southwest Corner" # -314333.57 3603628.25 101.98 # facing front: -0.77 back: 2.38
# W track bumps: "Road Bumps" # -314344.58 3603665.72 101.99 # facing front: -0.02 back: 3.12
# NW corner of track: "Northwest Corner" # -314339.64 3603769.53 101.98 # facing frpmt" -0.04 back: 3.11
# Center of gun firing berm line: "Armor Firing Range." # -314306.27 3603792.69 102.06 # facing front: 0.07 back: -3.07
4.0.label = The Tank Commander
4.1.label = Turn off your Engine 4.1.alert = In combat, it is wise to turn off your engine when not maneuvering. This will allow you to hear enemy tanks moving up and they will not be able to hear you.[NL][NL]Turn off your engine using {engstart}. 4.1.alert.camera = internal
4.2.label = Move to the Commander 4.2.alert = The second position in this tank is the Tank Commander. Tank Commanders usually have a better view than the other positions.[NL][NL]Press {positiontwo} to switch to the commander position. 4.2.complete.modal = If you switch positions away from the Driver, the vehicle will continue with the last input it had. Thus, if you were holding down the gas, the vehicle will continue to move forward when you switch to another position. This can be dangerous at times because it is difficult for the tank to remain straight due to the terrain.
4.3.label = The Commander's View 4.3.alert = The commander's view is limited to a small foward view port. However, the commander can open the top hatch of the turret, or "unbutton," to get a much wider view.[NL][NL]In the Panzer 38(t), the commander is also the gunner. The functions change based on whether the commander's hatch is open, which "unbuttons" the position.[NL][NL]Press {canopycontrol} to open the commander's hatch. 4.3.complete.modal = Control the commander's view by steering it with {turretraverse} and {turretelevate}. Notice that this moves the entire turret.
4.4.label = Use Your Binoculars 4.4.alert = View your surroundings through the commander's binoculars.[NL][NL]Press {instrumentview} to bring up your binoculars.
4.5.label = Look Around 4.5.alert = Take a moment to look North down the gun range at the dirt mounds with targets on them.
4.6.label = Button Up 4.6.alert = Press {instrumentview} to return to normal view. Then press {canopycontrol} to close the commander's hatch.
5.0.label = The Gunner's View
5.1.label = Move to the Gun 5.1.alert.modal = This is the same position as the commander but now functions as the gunner. The view is very limited except through his gunsight. From the gunner's position, you can fire the main gun and the turret's coaxial machine gun.
5.2.label = The Gunner's View 5.2.alert = As the gunner, this position has a magnified view through the gunsight.[NL][NL]Press {gunsightview} to cycle through the gunsight views.
5.3.label = Move the Turret 5.3.alert = Just like the commander's view, the turret can be moved with {turretraverse} and {turretelevate}.[NL][NL]Try moving the turret around. 5.3.complete.modal = The turret can be moved 360 degrees around the tank!
5.4.label = Fire the Main Gun 5.4.alert = Take a moment to fire the main gun down range.[NL][NL]Press {primarytrigger.1} to fire the main gun. 5.4.complete.modal = Use the main gun to take out other vehicles and buildings.
5.5.label = Fire the Machinegun 5.5.alert = Now fire the machine gun down range.[NL][NL]Press {secondarytrigger.1} to fire the turret's coaxial machine gun. 5.5.complete.modal = Use your machine gun against infantry and soft targets like trucks.
6.0.label = Gunnery
6.1.label = Shoot the Left Target 6.1.alert.modal = The Panzer 38(t)'s gunsight is the 7 small triangles near the center of the view. It is set to aim at the top of the center triangle. The range setting is indicated at the top of the view where the small vertical line intersects the ring of numbers (hundreds of meters). You can adjust the gunsight with {gunsightrangeinc} and {gunsightrangedec}. 6.1.alert1 = Fire the main gun at the far left target using {primarytrigger.1}. It is approximately 200 meters away. 6.1.complete = Well done, you hit the target!
6.2.label = The Gunsight 6.2.alert.modal = The target is easy to hit because it is close, but farther targets require you adjust your aim because the shell drops due to gravity. 6.2.alert1 = Try to hit the next target to the right, which is approximately 500 meters distant.[NL][NL]Use {gunsightrangeinc} and {gunsightrangedec} to set the gunsight's range to be about 500.[NL][NL]Shoot the 500 meter target. 6.2.complete.modal = Well done. If the distance is known, it is easy to adjust your gunsight to hit the target.
6.3.label = Sight Adjustment 6.3.alert.modal = Now try to hit a harder target. The two right targets are pretty far out. Try to hit one adjusting your sights as needed. 6.3.alert1 = First, fire your main gun at one to see where your round lands.[NL][NL]If it falls short, adjust your aim up. If it goes long, adjust your aim down. 6.3.complete.modal = Nice shot! As you can see, those targets are about 1000 meters away. Typically, armored vehicle combat takes place between 500 and 2000 meters.[NL][NL]In the Panzer 38(t) the gunsight is not effective for the coaxial machine gun, so you must estimate this yourself.
6.4.label = Main Gun Ammo 6.4.alert = Many tanks have different ammo types available for the main gun. You can switch ammo types using {cycleammo}.[NL][NL]Use {cycleammo} to switch your main gun to using high-explosive (HE) ammunition. 6.4.alert.hilite = primary,target 6.4.complete.modal = Use armor piercing (AP) rounds to penetrate the armor of enemy tanks. Use high-explosive (HE) rounds to destroy softer targets like trucks and troops. 6.4.complete.hilite = primary,target
6.5.label = Fire HE 6.5.alert = Fire a few of these rounds and notice how they behave differently from the armor piercing (AP) rounds in flight and in impact.[NL][NL]When you are ready to continue, switch to the hull gunner's position {positionfour}.
6.6.label = Hull Gunner 6.6.alert = The Panzer 38(t) has a hull gunner position that controls a machine gun mounted on the front of the tank.[NL][NL]Press {gunsightview} to cycle through the gunsight views.
6.7.label = Fire Hull Gun 6.7.alert = Move the gun and change the gunsight range the same as you would the tank's main gun.[NL][NL]Press {primarytrigger.1} to fire the machine guns. 6.8.label = Select Driver 6.8.alert = Good. This weapon can be effective at close range when you are facing soft targets in front of you.[NL][NL]Now switch to the driver's position {positionone}.
7.0.label = Complete the Course
7.1.label = Start Your Engine 7.1.alert = Start your engine using {engstart} and zoom into the driver's view port using {gunsightview}.
7.2.label = Reverse 7.2.alert = Tanks can also drive in reverse, which is often very helpful. Use {reverse} to toggle between forward and reverse gears.[NL][NL]When you press {reverse}, your tank's gear will automatically be set to neutral.[NL][NL]Put your tank in reverse. 7.2.alert.hilite = readout,target
7.3.label = Shift into Gear 7.3.alert = You still need to shift into reverse; do so by pressing {shiftup}. 7.3.alert.hilite = readout,target
7.4.label = Back Out 7.4.alert = Back out onto the road. Give your tank some gas using {gas.10.4} and turn left using {leftbrake.10.4} until you can see the road.[NL][NL]Once the road is in sight, use {bothbrake.10.4} to stop the tank. Use {reverse} to re-engage the forward gears. 7.4.alert.hilite = readout,target
7.5.label = Drive Home 7.5.alert = Shift into first gear using {shiftup}.[NL][NL]Now follow the waypoints back to the beginning.[NL][NL]Use {gas.10.4} to accelerate.[NL]Use {bothbrake.10.4} to brake.[NL]Use {leftbrake.10.4} and {rightbrake.10.4} to steer left and right. 7.5.alert.hilite = readout,target
8.0.label = Complete
8.1.label = Tutorial Completed 8.1.alert.modal = Well done! You have completed the basic armor tutorial.
